doc.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015

title: Basie in decline and studying the book
summary: Basie in a wheelchair after a stroke; Eddie had memorized most of the book from records.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Basie was in his declining years?

Yeah. He was in a wheelchair. I think he’d had a stroke in about 1979 — 78 or 79. Butch was on the band at the time. And that was when I really became a fan of the band. When my teacher got the gig with the Basie band it was like whoa. So then I immersed myself in the Basie things. I bought all the old records like “April in Paris” and “Standing Ovation,” “Live at Birdland,” all of that stuff. “Atomic Basie.” And I just studied it and studied it. I had 95% of the book memorized when I got there.
